title: The preference is bound to a user id and validated by the team request's own authorization
context: The user id is unknown at cold start, because it comes from a request the preference exists to avoid waiting for. GET /api/teams/:id already requires the caller to be a member of that team, so asking for the preferred team also asks the server whether the user still belongs to it.
decision: The preference stores the user id it was written for and is used at once as the team to request. A successful team request confirms membership. When the request is refused, or useUser answers with a different user id, the preference is discarded and the existing full resolution runs and its result is stored. Sign-out always clears it. Before verification only a team id is sent, and no team data is shown.

alternatives.option: Wait for useUser before using the preference
alternatives.reason: It puts back the round trip the preference exists to remove, to guard against exposing a team id that the server refuses to answer for a non-member anyway.

alternatives.option: Verify membership from the players list before requesting the team
alternatives.reason: That list needs the user id first, which rebuilds the dependent chain.

consequences: A preference that points at a team the user has left costs one refused request before the fallback.
The sign-out handler in src/components/user/index.tsx must clear the preference before it navigates away.
The team tab's root route must follow the resolved team, because it is currently decided once.
revisitTriggers: The preference starts to hold more than a team id.
